that proof establishes
$$v\in X_i=A_i\cup F_i$$
for its original owner, and then excludes the regular  $2P1T$  terminal alternative  $F_i$ . Consequently, the endpoint  $v$  itself is the upper corner  $A_i$ . The pair therefore fixes the bar direction as rightward. The perpendicular direction into the second bar row and near leg must be downward: the upward direction would occupy the finally blank gate  $u=(2,2)$ . The complete bar contains
$$\{(3,c):2\le c\le v+1\},\qquad v\ge6.$$
In particular it contains  $(3,6)$ , which is an original endpoint of the positive right leg because  $b\ge4$ .If the upper corner is  $\zeta=(2,3)$ , the pair fixes the bar direction as downward. The near leg must run rightward, since the leftward direction would occupy  $u$ . Its endpoint segment contains
$$\{(2,c):3\le c\le h+3\},\qquad h\ge4,$$
and hence contains the original positive endpoint  $(2,6)$ .Both are contradictions to original endpoint disjointness. Reflection excludes blank right marks.This proves the claimed scope: every actual width-six mark has an occupied gate, regardless of whether the positive is singly or doubly marked, its terminal activation count, its leg heights, or the reserve.2. \qquad
F_{\leftarrow}(r,c)=(k+2-r,6-c).$$

hence
